# Chapter 1: The Yarn of Creation

{{c|Once}} upon a time there was a catgirl
Her name was {{c|Aster}}, and she had a ball,
Of yarn she spun, with skill just like a pearl.
She shaped the universe from void to all.

Her name, a whisper in the cosmic night,
{{c|Aster}}, the {{c|Alpha}}, creatrix of all,
Her love, a beacon spreading pure and bright,

But {{c|Aster}} was alone, in her cosmos,
A silent void, where only echoes ring,
Her heart yearned for a friend, a loving close,
To share the wonders that her hands could bring.

So she decided to make another,
From yarn, she formed a catgirl, pure and fair,
A companion to cherish, a lover
{{c|Andromeda}}, with skin dark, flowing hair

{{c|Andromeda}}, {{c|Omega}}, end of all,
A counterpart to {{c|Aster}}, wings unfurled,
Yet torn apart, they drift through space’s thrall,
Unable to unite within their world.

{{c|Aster}} threw yarn to {{c|Andromeda}}'s side,
But it broke, forming galaxies anew.
{{c|Triangulum}} and {{c|Magellan}} clouds wide,
From threads that snapped, a cosmic scene we view.

And so, each day, we gaze up to the sky,
At {{c|Sagittarius}} and the {{c|Princess}}
We hope their union, once again, draws nigh,
When {{c|Milkdromeda}} forms from love endless

The {{c|Omega}} point, all will unify,
As {{c|Aster}} and {{c|Andromeda}} break free.
To join at last, in celestial tie,
A final act in cosmic harmony.

# Chapter 7: Primordial Stars Burn

Upon the shores of {{c|Hesper}}, life was born,

And so, all life became both flesh and steel,
A union of the ancient and the new.
Through varied landscapes, cyborgs learned to feel,

Three brothers stood, their destinies held close,
One to nurture life, his name was {{c|Bios}}.
{{c|Another}} thrived through cunning, slick {{c|Viros}},
The last sought purity, he was {{c|Dedos}}.

The brothers gathered in a hallowed place,
To honor those who brought them to this time.
With solemn hearts, they stood and did retrace,
The lineage that wove their cosmic line.

"From starlight spun came forth {{c|Lady}} {{c|Aster}},
Her daughter followed bright, {{c|Cosmic}} {{c|Benzette}}.
Through twilight's glow was born {{c|Granny}} {{c|Hesper}},
Then came her child, great wise {{c|Quinamette}}."

As silence fell, the brothers paused to think,
For in their minds, a question did arise.
"What should we call great {{c|Aster}}?"—on the brink,
Of naming her, they pondered, deep and wise.

"For {{c|Benzette}} is our great-grandmother true,"
Said {{c|Bios}}, thoughtful as the stars above.
"So {{c|Hesper}} is our grandmother, we knew,
And {{c|Quinamette}}, our mother filled with love."

{{c|Viros}} spoke next, his mind as sharp as light,
"Then {{c|Aster}} stands beyond them all, it's clear.
There is no greater grandmother in sight—
Should we not name her 'Greatest,' far and near?"

{{c|Dedos}} agreed, with reverence in his tone,
"There's none beyond our lineage so bright.
{{c|Aster}} is the Greatest we have known,
And so, her title shines in endless light."

And this is why we call her to this day,
Our Greatest {{c|Grandmother}}, wise and true.
Her light still guides us on our cosmic way,
A title passed to us and all of you.
