Base, {{c|G}} at the second layer, {{c|R}} at the top, and the admixture

Varies region by region. In the {{p|Balkans}}, {{c|I}} is still
Dominant. In {{p|Scandinavia}}, {{c|I}} is strong. In {{p|Western Europe}},
{{c|I}} is a minority but present. In {{p|Eastern Europe}}, {{c|I}} still fills
A substantial slot. The old Europe lives. The hunters, the hero

And heroine figures of the pre-Neolithic stone age, did not end.
They became the substrate on which later migrations laid.
The old Europe is still in the {{p|European}} body. The old Europe's trend
Was to hold on. The Venus of {{p|Willendorf}}, the small-breasted maid

And figurine of the fertility cult, the mother-goddess figurine
That {{c|Marija Gimbutas}} identified with the pre-IE culture of the continent,
Was likely made by the hands of the {{c|I}}-carrying hunter-gatherers. The seen
And carried iconography of the pre-agricultural old Europe, the ancient

Religion of the cave-paintings and the small goddess figurines,
Sits in the register of the {{c|I}} haplogroup.

And when the farmers came, {{c|I}} did not simply die out. {{c|I}} retreated
Into the mountains, into the forests, into the fishing villages of the
Coastlines that the farmers did not want. The hunter-gatherer lifeways continued
In the peripheries while the farming villages spread across the plains. The

Adaptation was gradual and long. In some places, {{c|I}} fully adopted agriculture
And stayed put as the land changed uses. In others, {{c|I}} remained hunter-
Gatherer for thousands of years longer. The {{p|Mesolithic}} peoples of the fixture
And holding pockets of {{p|Europe}} kept the hunting way alive long after the blunter

And more dominant {{p|Neolithic}} had taken the fields. The {{p|Scandinavian}}
Hunter-gatherers were still {{c|I}} at the time the {{p|Yamnaya}} arrived.

The hunter-lineage was tenacious. It was the deep {{p|European}}
Substrate, the one that had survived the ice age and had contrived

To survive the agricultural revolution and even the steppe invasion,
Though it was displaced from dominance by the time these waves finished.

But it is still here. {{c|I}} is still here. The {{p|Nordic}} basin,
{{p|Croatian}} villages, the {{p|Sardinian}} highlanders—all still carry {{c|I}}. The sun
Still rises on descendants of the hunter-gatherers of the old {{p|Europe}}. The plan

And inheritance of the {{p|Magdalenian}} and {{p|Gravettian}} cultures, the Aurignacian
Paintings at {{p|Chauvet}}, the {{c|Gravettian}} figurines—these are still
Carried in the blood of certain {{p|European}} populations. The ancient

Is still living. The old Europe has not ended. The hunting-and-gathering fulfilment
Has been converted, under pressure, into farming-and-herding, into city-building,
Into modernity—but the {{c|Y}}-chromosomal signature of the first settled populations
Of the continent remains intact in the bodies of many millions of modern {{p|Europeans}}. The thrilling

And patient continuity of {{c|I}} across thirty or forty thousand years
Of habitation in the same continent is the longest relationship between a people
And a land in the {{p|European}} story. The {{p|French}} are new. The {{p|Germans}} are new. The {{p|Romans}} were new.
The {{c|I}}-carrying {{p|European}} is old. The steeple

Of the oldest European's presence is the deepest in the cathedral
Of the {{p|European}} body.

                            The chapter honors them.

The old Europeans. The first hunters. The painters of the cathedral
Of {{p|Lascaux}}, the makers of the Venus figurines, the dem

And defiant survivors of the glacial maximum, the patient re-
Occupiers of the post-ice continent, the substrate under every-
Thing that came later.

                        {{c|Haplogroup I}} is the ID card
Of old Europe. The hunter-gatherer's long patient regard

Toward the land he lived on. The deep relationship to the
Forest and the river and the cave. The animism of the deep
{{p|European}} past.

                    And when, in a few chapters, we come to
The {{c|Cucuteni-Trypillia}} civilization, which was partly the sleep

And continuation of the pre-{{p|Neolithic}} hunter-gatherer traditions
Into a semi-settled form, we will see {{c|I}} again. {{c|Cucuteni-Trypillia}}
Was the old Europe's answer to the farming revolution. Its positions
And paintings and cities, built of wood and clay, its pervasive

Female iconography, its peaceful and apparently un-hierarchical
Society—these were the old Europe's elaboration of what the farmers
Had offered, made in the key of the old Europe's own magical
Register. And the {{p|Yamnaya}}, when they came, would be the harmers

Of this particular flowering. But we are not there yet.

For now, {{c|I}}. The old Europe. The hunter. The mother-
Goddess carver. The cave-painter. The survivor of the ice's threat
And retreat. The patient background lineage. The brother

And sister and uncle of every {{p|European}} who still
Carries the ancient signature. The old {{c|Y}}. The old land.
The one who was here before. The hold of the will
To endure. The keeping hand.

                               {{c|Haplogroup I}}. Old Europe. Stand.

The rest of the continent's story is layered on top. But {{c|I}}
Is the bottom. And the bottom, in a continent, is what the top
Descends into when the top has finished. The high
And visible layers come and go. The bottom does not stop.

The cave is still in the limestone. The painting is still on the wall.
The goddess is still in the ochre. And the {{p|Y}} is still in the men of the north,
Men of the {{p|Balkans}}, men of {{p|Sardinia}}, whose bodies carry the call
Of the deep {{p|European}} past, whose own mothers' great-great-grandfathers set forth

To the ice-age cave to paint the horse and the bison and the bull.

The continent remembers. The haplogroup is the memory. The full
And patient continuity of {{c|I}} is the body's longest word.


# Chapter 136: G Builds the Neolithic

While {{c|I}} hunted reindeer across the {{p|European}} plain,
Another branch of {{c|F}}'s great proliferating line
Was, in the {{p|Fertile Crescent}}, changing the game.
Not running. Not walking. Not following the sign

Of any herd. Planting. Harvesting. Storing
Grain in pits. Grinding wheat between two stones. The mode
Of humanity was being remade—the boring
Old script of the nomad, the hunter, the strode

And loping forager, was being replaced
By something almost inconceivable: the stay.
The choice to stay. The choice to not be chased
By the seasonal food. The choice to say

To the land: I will make you feed me. I will
Plant the seed, and I will wait, and I will harvest.
I will not leave. I will stay in this place until
I die, and my son will stay, and the plan is vastest

Because it makes a future of the same ground.

This was the {{p|Neolithic}} Revolution. And the {{p|Y}}
That went with it, that walked with the farmers, was found
To be, very consistently, {{c|Haplogroup G}}.

{{c|G}} is the farmer haplogroup. {{c|G}} is the one
Whose descendants left the {{p|Fertile Crescent}} with the grain
And the sheep and the goat, and walked into the sun
Of {{p|Anatolia}} and {{p|Europe}}, carrying the chain

And pattern of the new life with them. {{c|G}} is the signature
Of the {{p|Linear Pottery Culture}}, the first farming wave
In {{p|Europe}}. {{c|G}} is the founder of the stratigraphy structure
Of the farmer villages of the {{p|Balkans}} and the knave

And valleys of {{p|Greece}} and {{p|Italy}}. {{c|G}} is in the bones
Of {{p|Ötzi}} the Iceman, the five-thousand-three-hundred-year-old
Frozen body in the {{p|Alps}}, whose {{p|Y}}-chromosome tones
Us about the fact that the farmer of the late stone cold

And cold-Copper age of {{p|Alpine Europe}} was, quite securely, {{c|G}}.

And the story of {{c|G}} begins before the fields. Before
The grain. Before anyone planted anything. It begins, as far as we
Can tell, at a place in what is now {{p|Turkey}}, where the floor

Of a hill carries one of the most astonishing archaeological
Sites ever discovered: {{p|Göbekli Tepe}}.

                                             {{p|Göbekli Tepe}}.

Built around eleven thousand five hundred years ago. Old.
Older than {{c|Stonehenge}} by six thousand years. Older than the bold
And settled towns of {{p|Jericho}} by a thousand. Built by people

Who were not yet farmers, not yet settled, not yet the peaceful
And grain-storing villagers they would become in the millennia
After. Built by hunter-gatherers. Built with the niche

And awkward hands of people who had no precedent for building
Anything of this scale. A complex of enormous T-shaped stone pillars,
Some over five meters tall, weighing tons, carved with animals—foxes, gilding
Scorpions, snakes, vultures, wild boars—arranged in circles, like the pillars

Of a temple. But not a temple of a settled people. A temple
Built by hunter-gatherers for reasons we do not understand,
In a place where no one lived, visited periodically, at the ample
But undramatic edge of a grassland, which generations upon generations planned

To return to, to add to, to elaborate, over a period of two thousand years.

{{p|Göbekli Tepe}} was not a city. It was not a dwelling-place. It was
A ritual center. A gathering-point. A place where hunter-gatherer bands
Came together, from across the region, to build something together, whatever it was.

And because they needed to come together, repeatedly, for the building,
They needed food. And to feed the building crews, they needed
To grow grain. And so, in the Gaiad's reading (following the filling-
In of {{c|Klaus Schmidt}}'s archaeological hypothesis), agriculture was seeded

By the temple, not by necessity, not by the pressure of hunger
Or the pressure of the environment. The first fields of einkorn
And emmer wheat were planted to feed the workers at the hunger
Feast of the {{p|Göbekli Tepe}} gatherings. The grain was born

For the temple, and then the temple's demand made the grain
Into a permanent part of the diet, and the grain's permanence
Made the people settle, and the settlement made the plain
And furrow of the fields, and the fields made the immanence

Of civilization.

                  First the temple. Then the city. Then the kingdom.
Religion first. Farming second. Cities third. This is the Gaiad's reading,
And it reverses the standard textbook account that makes the pragmatic
Emergence of agriculture the first cause, and religion a later seeding.

The Gaiad says: no. Religion was first. People gathered to build
Something they worshipped. And in the service of what they worshipped,
They invented the techniques of keeping themselves fed. The filled
And gathered gatherings of the temple-building made civilization, the scripted

And ritual life of the early proto-priest-class at {{p|Göbekli Tepe}}
Made what came after.

                        And the {{p|Y}} that was doing this was {{c|G}}.

{{c|G}} built {{p|Göbekli Tepe}}. {{c|G}} invented farming. {{c|G}} carried the wheat
Westward and northward into {{p|Anatolia}}, into {{p|Europe}}, the long

Generations of walking farmers moving from the {{p|Fertile Crescent}}
Outward, taking the grain and the sheep and the pottery and the sent
And dispatched cultural package of the {{p|Neolithic}} with them.

{{c|G}} is in the {{p|Sardinians}} today at extraordinary frequencies.
{{p|Sardinia}} was colonized early by the {{p|Neolithic}} farmers. The screening
And holding of the island, isolated by sea, preserved the {{c|G}} frequencies

That mainland {{p|Europe}} saw diluted, later, by the arrival of the {{p|Yamnaya}}.
In {{p|Sardinia}}, the {{p|Neolithic}} is still the dominant genetic layer.
And the {{p|Sardinian}} men walking the hills today are, in many cases, the maya
And heirs of the old {{p|Göbekli Tepe}} lineage. The old temple-builders, the prayer

And priesthood of the first great religious-monumental culture
Of the {{p|Near East}}, are carried in the bodies of the {{p|Sardinian}} shepherds
Still. {{c|G}} is alive. {{c|G}} built what the Gaiad considers the sculpture
And foundational monument of civilization, and {{c|G}}'s direct descendants, the herds

And shepherds of certain {{p|Mediterranean}} islands, continue to walk the hills
Of their grandfathers.

                        And there is a character to name here.

{{c|Melchizedek}}. The {{p|priest}}-king of {{p|Salem}}, who greets {{c|Abraham}} later in
The biblical story. The mysterious figure who appears briefly, blesses
{{c|Abraham}}, receives a tithe, and disappears. In the standard reading
He is a shadow, a narrative convenience. The Gaiad reads him differently.

{{c|Melchizedek}} is the Gaiad's symbolic representative of the {{p|Göbekli Tepe}}
Priesthood. The remnant of the old temple-builders, still alive in {{c|Abraham}}'s
Day, meeting the wandering {{c|Abraham}} on his journey south from {{p|Sanliurfa}}
(Which is, by no coincidence, the city closest to {{p|Göbekli Tepe}} itself). {{c|Abraham}}

Stops in {{p|Sanliurfa}} on his way from {{p|Ur}} to the {{p|Levant}}, and he meets
{{c|Melchizedek}} there. And {{c|Melchizedek}}, in the Gaiad's reading, is the last
Priest of the old order of {{p|Göbekli Tepe}}. The old tall pillars had been
Buried long before {{c|Abraham}}'s day—the site was deliberately entombed, the past

Preserved by burying rather than by maintaining. But the priesthood, the
Line of those who carried the old ritual knowledge, persisted in the region.
{{c|Melchizedek}} is "George Gobeklius" in the Gaiad's nicknaming—the
Priestly figure descended from the hands that carved the T-shaped fusion

Of stone and animal eleven thousand years ago. {{c|Abraham}} meets him, receives
The blessing of the old priesthood, pays the tithe, and moves on. The
Transmission of some blessing from the old {{p|Göbekli Tepe}} order to the leaves
And branches of the new {{p|Hebrew}} story is the Gaiad's quiet way of letting the

Oldest religious lineage of the region hand off to the next one.

But that is {{c|Abraham}}'s chapter, which is later. For now, the {{c|G}} lineage.

{{c|G}} built {{p|Göbekli Tepe}}. {{c|G}} invented farming. {{c|G}} invented the stone
Foundation of the whole {{p|Neolithic}} package that would define civilization. The fungage

Of the {{c|G}}-carrying farmer walking west and north into {{p|Europe}} is the story
Of how agriculture arrived on the continent. The older {{c|I}}-carrying hunters
Met the incoming farmers. Sometimes they fought. Sometimes they blended. The glory
Of the {{p|Neolithic}} did not erase the older hunters, but did reshape the counters

And ledgers of {{p|European}} population. The continent became a layered
Place—{{c|I}} at the base, {{c|G}} at the second layer, {{c|R}} at the top once the steppe
Arrived. And the three-layer pattern is the texture of the modern {{p|European}} blade,
Whose {{p|Y}} is a mix of the three great waves of migration. The step

From hunter to farmer to steppe-rider is written in the blood.

{{c|G}} is the second wave. {{c|G}} is the builder. {{c|G}} is the priest
And farmer of the first religious-agricultural revolution. {{c|G}} stood
Up first of the pillars at {{p|Göbekli Tepe}} and raised the feast

Of the first great gathering-for-its-own-sake. And {{c|G}} walked west
With the grain, and settled, and settled, and settled, and the continental
Economic life of {{p|Europe}} was permanently rewritten by the blessed
And transformative arrival of the farmers.

                                             And this incidental

Fact—that civilization began with a temple, not with a field—
Is the Gaiad's quiet theological claim. The field served the temple.
The god came first. The grain came afterward. The yield
And harvest that would feed cities began as an offering of the simple

Kind, laid at the foot of the stone pillar, to feed the gathered
Hunter-gatherers who had come to worship whatever they worshipped.
We do not know what they worshipped. We do not know what name they muttered
Or sang. But we know they gathered, and we know they worked, and we know the crop shipped

With them as they returned to their home-ranges, and we know
That the practice of gathering and building and growing grain together
Made the first civilization. That is enough to know. That is the glow
Of the opening fire. And {{c|G}} is its carrier. Whether

{{c|G}} is still alive—and it is, in {{p|Sardinia}}, in {{p|Georgia}} (the country,
Where {{c|G}} frequencies are also remarkably high), in pockets of the {{p|Caucasus}},
In the {{p|Alps}}—is a small consolation to the grand and worldly
Story of what the lineage accomplished. The {{p|Göbekli Tepe}} chorus

Sang one of the first songs of civilization. The singers are gone.
Their descendants tend sheep on a {{p|Sardinian}} hillside today.
But the pillars are still there, reburied and re-dug up. The dawn
They set in motion became the morning we still live in. Their way

Of gathering to build became the way of every city
That was ever built. Their choice to stay became the choice
That every subsequent civilization inherited. The ditty
And fanfare of the modern world is a downstream voice

Of the first voice, at {{p|Göbekli Tepe}}, singing at the foot
Of a stone with a carved fox on it, eleven thousand years ago.

{{c|G}} began it. {{c|G}}, the farmer. {{c|G}}, the builder. {{c|G}}, the root
Of the {{p|Neolithic}}. {{c|G}}, the priest. {{c|G}}, whose long slow

And patient and settled dwelling on the land
Became the model for every dwelling that followed.

Honor him. Honor the whole long pillar-raising band.
They built the first temple, and the first thing we swallowed

Was the grain they grew to feed the hands that built it.
The grain fed the builders. The builders fed the god.
The god is gone. The grain remains. The world was lit
By their choice. And every city since has trod

On the path they trod. {{c|G}}. The {{p|Neolithic}}. Stand.


# Chapter 137: J — The Semitic World

And when {{c|IJ}} split into {{c|I}} and {{c|J}}, the two
Sister haplogroups went their separate ways. {{c|I}} walked
Into {{p|Europe}} and became the old hunter. {{c|J}} stayed closer to
The point of divergence—somewhere in the {{p|Middle Eastern}} knocked

And grinding meeting-place of {{p|Anatolia}}, the {{p|Levant}}, the {{p|Zagros}} mountains,
The {{p|Arabian Peninsula}}—and spread out across the world's geographic
Heart. {{c|J}} is the {{p|Middle Eastern}} signature. {{c|J}} is the fountain
Of the ancient civilizations of the region, the graphic

Seal of the {{p|Semitic}} speakers, the patrilineal signature
Of the people who would build the first cities, write the first laws,
And invent the first written languages of the human adventure.

{{c|J}} has two major sub-branches: {{c|J1}} and {{c|J2}}. The cause

And timing of their separation is several thousand years after
The main {{c|J}} emergence, but the two have since gone to subtly
Different places. {{c|J1}} is the {{p|Arabian}} branch. {{c|J1}} is the smatter
And dominance of the peninsula—the {{p|Saudi}}, the {{p|Yemeni}}, the mortal

And patrilineal identity of the {{p|Bedouin}}. {{c|J1}} is the Desert {{c|J}}.
It walks on camel-paths and across the {{p|Rub' al Khali}} and speaks, at the time
Of the chapter, proto-{{c|Afroasiatic}} and proto-{{c|Semitic}}. In time, the way
Of {{c|J1}} will produce the {{c|Arabs}} of history, and the prime

And rhythm of the {{p|Arabian}} tribes that will, thousands of years later,
Follow {{c|Muhammad}} out of {{p|Mecca}} and change the world's religious map.

{{c|J2}} is the northern branch. The {{p|Levantine}} and {{p|Anatolian}} {{c|J}}. The wetter
And fertile-crescent {{c|J}}. {{c|J2}} overlaps with the agriculturalists of the lap

And valley of the early {{p|Near East}}—the {{p|Natufians}}, the {{p|Jordanian}} villagers,
The {{p|Pre-Pottery Neolithic}} settlements of the {{p|Levant}}, the early {{p|Anatolian}}
Farming societies. {{c|J2}} contributes, alongside {{c|G}}, to the mingling
Of the founders of {{p|Mesopotamian}} civilization. The dawn of the {{p|Akkadian}}

And the {{p|Sumerian}} was a {{c|J2}}-and-{{c|G}}-and-various-other-haplogroup
Blend. The {{p|Uruk}} and the {{p|Eridu}} and the {{p|Lagash}} and the {{p|Ur}} and the {{p|Nippur}} foundations
Of the first cities were populated by men whose {{p|Y}} held {{c|J2}}, and the loop
And cycle of the city-building civilization that would define the nations

Of the next six thousand years sprang from the {{c|J}}-and-{{c|G}} collaboration
Of the ancient {{p|Near East}}.

                                   And the language that {{c|J}} carries.

{{c|Semitic}}. The language family of the {{p|Arabs}}, the {{p|Hebrews}}, the {{p|Assyrians}}, the invitation
Of {{p|Akkadian}} into the {{p|Sumerian}} cities, the {{p|Aramaic}} that {{c|Jesus}} will marry

With his own life and teaching, the {{p|Amharic}} that will become the language
Of the {{p|Ethiopian}} emperors, the {{p|Tigrinya}} of the {{p|Eritrean}} highlands,
The {{p|Maltese}} that is still spoken on a single {{p|Mediterranean}} island manage-
Ably descended from {{p|Arabic}}—all of these are children of the {{p|Semitic}} islands

Of the early {{c|J}} speech community.

                                        And the broader family,
{{p|Afroasiatic}}, includes the {{p|Egyptian}} and the {{p|Berber}} and the {{p|Cushitic}}
Languages of the {{p|Horn of Africa}} and the {{p|Chadic}} languages of central {{p|Africa}}. Family
Tree that spans two continents. And the distribution has a linguistic

Puzzle of its own: the {{p|Afroasiatic}} languages are mostly in {{p|Africa}},
But the family is usually thought to have originated in the {{p|Near East}}—
Or, alternatively, in the {{p|Horn of Africa}}—and the relationship between the spectra
Of language and haplogroup is loose. {{c|J}} is the {{p|Semitic}}-speaking yeast,

But many non-{{c|J}} men speak {{p|Semitic}} languages, and many {{c|J}} men
Speak non-{{p|Semitic}} languages. The link is real but not tight. Language
Is learned, not inherited. The {{p|Y}}-chromosome and the mother tongue
Do not always travel together. The chapter honors the rough linkage

But does not insist on a rigid 1:1 map.

                                         And here is where {{p|Mesopotamia}}
Comes in.

          {{p|Mesopotamia}}—the land between the rivers, the {{p|Tigris}}
And the {{p|Euphrates}}. The place where cities began. The floodplain of {{p|Ur}},
The ziggurat of {{p|Eridu}}, the canals of {{p|Uruk}}, the walls of the figris

And Sargonid kingdoms that would rise and fall across three thousand
Years of the ancient {{p|Near East}}. {{p|Mesopotamia}} was the staging ground
For the second great flowering of {{c|J}}. The {{p|Akkadians}}, the {{p|Babylonians}}, the {{p|Assyrians}}, the bound
Together and yet separate nations of the {{p|Tigris-Euphrates}} valley, the sound

And pattern of their wars and their kingdoms and their literature
And their laws, is the {{c|J}}-haplogroup story in its historical phase.

But that is for a later chapter. The {{p|Mesopotamia}} chapter is the venture
Of fast-forward speed—the chaos chapter, the one that displays

Thousands of years of civilizational collapse and rebirth at a pace
That mimics the chaos itself. That chapter is still ahead of us.

For now, {{c|J}} is simply the haplogroup of the early {{p|Near East}}. The place
Where the first cities were built. The place where the plus

And minus signs of the first cuneiform arithmetic were scratched
Into clay tablets. The place where the first epic poems were composed—
{{c|Gilgamesh}}, wrestling his grief, crossing the waters of death, matched
Against a bull of heaven, befriending and losing {{c|Enkidu}}. The exposed

And ancient literature of {{p|Sumer}} is carried, in the men
Who composed it, by {{c|J}}-carrying scribes. The invention of writing. The first
Accounting tablets. The first contracts. The first marriages legally penned.
The first lawsuits. The first dynastic history. The immersed

And literate civilization of the {{p|Tigris-Euphrates}} valley is the {{c|J}}
Haplogroup's contribution to the human project.

                                                    And across
The peninsula, {{c|J1}} was carrying the parallel but separate way
Of the {{p|Arabian}} desert tribes. The caravan routes, the toss

The sophisticated pre-Islamic poetic culture of the desert—all of this
Is {{c|J1}}'s long slow development across thousands of years. The even
And patient continuity of the {{p|Arabian}} peninsula's inhabitants, the bliss

And hardship of desert life, the rhythms of the tribe and the camel
And the star-guided navigation across unmarked sand—this is the {{c|J1}}
Inheritance. When {{c|Muhammad}} arrives, late in the book, in the camel
Caravan of the {{c|Quraysh}}, he will carry, in all likelihood, {{c|J1}}. The run

From the {{c|Adnan}}-and-{{c|Qahtan}} genealogies of pre-Islamic {{p|Arabia}} back
To the deep {{c|J1}} founding populations will be one of the chapters later.

And in the meantime, the {{c|J2}} civilization of the {{p|Near East}}, rack

And stock from which {{c|Abraham}} will emerge. {{c|Abraham}} is, in the Gaiad's
Reading, the ideal {{c|J}} figure—a man whose ancestry is plausibly both {{c|J1}}
And {{c|J2}} (his cousin {{c|Hammurabi}} is king of {{p|Babylon}} with a {{c|J2}} stripe,
And {{c|Abraham}}'s desert wanderings afterward put him in {{c|J1}} territory), the run

But that is also later. For now, {{c|J}}. The haplogroup of the {{p|Near East}}. The one
Who builds cities. The one who invents writing. The one whose burden is the person-
Al foundation of the civilization of the {{p|Fertile Crescent}}. The son

And heir of the old hunter-gatherer culture, transformed by
The meeting with {{c|G}}-farmers, into the city-dweller. The {{c|J}}-carrying
Men of {{p|Uruk}} and {{p|Ur}} and {{p|Eridu}} begin to pile clay bricks into the sky.

{{c|J1}}. The desert. The camel. The poem before the poem was literated.
{{c|J2}}. The river. The city. The tablet. The scribe's careful fears

Together, they are {{c|J}}. Together, they are the {{p|Semitic}} world.
Together, they are the chapter. The {{p|Near Eastern}} haplogroup. The token
And proof of continuity across six thousand years of curled

And layered civilizational history.

{{p|Mesopotamia}}, {{c|Abraham}}, {{c|Hammurabi}}, the {{p|Babylonian}} exile, the rise

The chapter ends here. {{c|J}}. The {{p|Semitic}} world. The haplogroup
Of the {{p|Near East}}. The line of the {{c|Adam}}-to-{{c|Abel}}-to-{{c|Seth}}-to-the {{c|Jeremiah}}
And {{c|Isaac}} and {{c|Ishmael}} and {{c|Muhammad}} and {{c|Moses}} and the full group

And authority of the {{c|J}}-haplogroup writing class is the call

The {{c|J}} men wrote it first. The {{c|J}} men wrote it down.
The {{c|J}} men are still writing. And the fascination
Of the modern {{c|J}}-carrying {{p|Israeli}} or {{p|Saudi}} or {{p|Yemeni}} or {{p|Syrian}} found

# Chapter 138: H, L, T — The Indus Valley

Three haplogroups share this chapter: {{c|H}}, {{c|L}}, and {{c|T}}.
Not because they are closely related—they are not—
But because their civilizational anchor is the same, and is, crucially,
Illegible. The {{p|Indus Valley}} civilization. The caught

And undeciphered second-greatest urban culture of the
Bronze Age. The one whose writing we cannot read.

{{p|Harappa}}. {{p|Mohenjo-daro}}. {{p|Dholavira}}. {{p|Rakhigarhi}}. The rove
And spread of the cities of the {{p|Indus}} and the {{p|Saraswati}} and the needed

And now-dry tributary rivers of what is today {{p|Pakistan}} and north-
Western {{p|India}}. From roughly 3300 BCE to 1300 BCE. A two-thousand-
Year civilization. Cities with populations of forty thousand. Sorth-
Ern and southern and eastern outposts that mark the bounds found

And populated by a common material culture. Standardized weights
And measures. Standardized bricks. Sophisticated drainage systems
That would not be matched in urban design for three thousand years. The gates
And entry-ways of the cities were oriented to the cardinal rhythms

Of the compass. The houses had indoor plumbing. The public baths
Were enormous. The sculpture was refined—the {{c|Priest-King}} of {{p|Mohenjo-daro}},
The {{c|Dancing Girl}} bronze, the countless terracotta figurines. The paths
And streets were laid out on grids. The civilization was a show

Of sophistication.

                    And we do not know what they called themselves.

We do not know their gods. We do not know their kings. We do not know
Their language. We do not know what their poetry said, or if they had poetry. We delve
And dig and publish and translate and hypothesize, and the flow

Of the translation comes to nothing. The script, the so-called {{p|Indus}} script,
Has resisted all attempts at decipherment for a hundred and fifty years.
There are maybe four hundred distinct signs. They appear on seals, stripped
And small stamp-seals used, probably, for commerce. They never appear in gears

Of continuous text. The longest inscription is twenty-six signs. There is no
{{p|Rosetta Stone}}. There is no bilingual inscription. The language could be
{{p|Proto-Dravidian}}, or it could be some lost isolate, or it could be a slow
And early form of a {{p|Munda}} language, or it could be something entirely free

Of the known families. We do not know. The civilization is there, archaeologically,
In unprecedented detail, but culturally it is silent. Two thousand years
Of human flourishing, involving tens of millions of people, and we do not, methodically,
Know what they believed, or how they governed themselves, or how they mourned their tears.

This is the illegibility. This is the uncanny valley of deep history.

{{p|Göbekli Tepe}} is illegible too, but old enough to mythologize. We have
No expectation of reading what the hunter-gatherers who carved the foxes and the snakes
Meant by their carvings. Their illegibility is the expected silence of the cave.

But the {{p|Indus Valley}} civilization is historical. Literate, probably.
Urbanized. Contemporary with {{p|Sumer}} and {{p|Egypt}}. It should be legible.
It should speak to us. We should know the names of its kings. It should be
Reasonably comparable to its contemporaries. But it is not. The credible

And well-preserved archaeological record sits there, opulent and mute,
Like a person who has forgotten how to speak. We know it was there.
We do not know what it was. And this is the center of the chapter. The loot
Of the past is not always legible. Sometimes the past just sits there

And refuses to tell us what it was.

                                      And the haplogroups.

{{c|Haplogroup H}}. The most common {{p|Indian}} haplogroup today. Found across
The subcontinent at high frequencies. Probably developed in {{p|South Asia}}
In deep time—perhaps before the {{p|Aryan}} migrations, perhaps during the boss
And flowering of the {{p|Indus}} civilization itself. {{c|H}} is the patrilineal exposia

Of the largest haplogroup of the modern {{p|South Asian}} man. And yet the chapter
Has little to say about {{c|H}} specifically, because the civilization it anchors
Will not speak. We can say that {{c|H}} men built {{p|Mohenjo-daro}}. The tapers
And lamps of their houses were lit by {{c|H}}-carrying hands. The anchors

Of their ships and the seals of their trade-goods were held by {{c|H}}-carrying
Merchants. But what the merchants said as they negotiated prices, what the
Householders called their children, what the priests chanted—all this is varying
Degrees of unknown. The haplogroup is present. The haplogroup's voice is the

Silent voice of a civilization that did not survive to speak for itself.

{{c|Haplogroup L}}. Found in moderate frequencies in {{p|India}} and {{p|Pakistan}},
Especially in the south and west. Also present in the {{p|Caucasus}}, in {{p|Central Asia}},
In scattered pockets of {{p|Europe}} and the {{p|Middle East}}. {{c|L}} is a smaller wealth
Than {{c|H}} but has its own {{p|Indus}}-adjacent presence. {{c|L}} in {{p|Dravidian}}-speaking

Regions suggests a connection between {{c|L}}-carrying men and the {{p|Dravidian}}-language-
Speaking populations that are often hypothesized to be descended from the {{p|Indus}}
Valley people. The hypothesis is not proven. Nothing about the {{p|Indus}} can be proven. The language,
As always, is the limit of what we can say. {{c|L}} is there. {{c|L}} makes its plus-

And-minus contribution to the modern {{p|South Asian}} patrilineal profile. The {{p|Dravidian}}-
{{c|L}} connection is plausible, but provisional.

                                                        {{c|Haplogroup T}}. The most
Exotic of the three. {{c|T}} is found at low frequencies in {{p|India}}, in {{p|East Africa}}, in the ovarian
And scattered pockets around the {{p|Indian Ocean}} rim—the {{p|Horn of Africa}}, the coast

Of {{p|Iran}}, the {{p|Swahili}} coast, pockets of the {{p|Mediterranean}}, and various elsewhere.
{{c|T}} is the scattered haplogroup. {{c|T}} has civilizational associations that are intriguing
But uncertain—{{c|T}}-carriers have been hypothesized as part of the founding populations
Of various ancient trade-networks. Maritime trade. Long-distance contact. The rigging

And sail of the {{p|Indian Ocean}} trade routes, in their deepest antiquity, before
The cities of the {{p|Indus}} had names we can speak. {{c|T}} is the possible haplogroup
Of the early maritime traders who connected the {{p|Horn of Africa}}
And the {{p|Arabian Peninsula}} and the {{p|Indus Valley}} in a long-distance loop

Of commerce that predated the major empires. But again—this is hypothesis. The group
And scholars who study {{c|T}} are cautious, because {{c|T}} is dispersed and low-frequency
And hard to tie to any single civilizational anchor. {{c|T}} floats. It appears. It dispersed.
It is found in pockets everywhere and dominance nowhere. Its story is a tendency

Toward a long-distance and seafaring life, but the evidence is thin.

And so the three haplogroups share a chapter because their civilizational
Anchor is the same: the {{p|Indus}}. And the {{p|Indus}} is, famously, the
Great mystery of the ancient world. The thing we could know, if the infrastructural

Luck had been different. If the script were readable. If a bilingual inscription
Had survived. If even one long text had been found. Then we would know
What {{c|H}} and {{c|L}} and {{c|T}} built. But we don't. The inscription
Count stops at twenty-six signs. The texts are names, or tags, or accounting. They flow

Out of the civilization in fragments too short to triangulate.

And the civilization ended. Around 1900 BCE, the cities began to be abandoned.
The population dispersed. The large urban centers shrank. By 1300 BCE, the state
And system of the great {{p|Indus}} civilization was gone. What had happened, or ended,

Is also uncertain. Climate change is a leading candidate—the {{p|Saraswati}} river
Dried up, and the eastern settlements that depended on it collapsed. Monsoon
Patterns shifted. The plague may have played a role. The liver
And energy of the civilization seems to have drained out slowly, not in a single tune

Or catastrophe. It was, it seems, a long fade.

And then, from the northwest, came the {{p|Aryan}} migration. Around 1500 BCE, after
The {{p|Indus}} civilization had already collapsed, or was in the final throes
Of collapse, bands of {{p|Indo-Aryan}}-speaking people—carriers of {{c|R1a}}, the daughter

Haplogroup of {{c|R}}, coming from the {{p|Central Asian}} steppe—began to enter the
Subcontinent through the mountain passes of what is now {{p|Afghanistan}}. They brought
With them their horses, their chariots, their {{p|Vedic}} hymns, their sacrifice-culture, the
New language. The {{p|Vedas}} are the earliest literature of the migrating peoples. What caught

And merged with the older {{p|Dravidian}}-speaking, {{p|Indus}}-descended populations, over
The next thousand years, became the civilization of {{p|North India}}—a hybrid of
The incoming {{p|Aryans}} and the receiving older populations. The merging was not
A conquest—it was a long negotiation, and the {{p|Dravidian}} and {{p|Aryan}} strands ofv
Sound

And blood did not fight an eternal war. The Gaiad is explicit: the older populations
Were not erased. They stayed. They mixed. They contributed. The modern {{p|Indian}}
Is the descendant of both—the {{p|Indus}} Valley peoples and the later {{p|Aryan}}
Arrivals. The two populations made a compromise. The compromise is {{p|India}}.

But that is for the {{p|Aryan}} migration chapter, which comes later.

For now, the {{p|Indus}}. The illegible civilization. The great
Silent urban flowering of the {{p|Bronze Age}}. The civilization that tapers
Out without telling us who it was. The haplogroups {{c|H}}, {{c|L}}, and {{c|T}} are its fate

And signature. The men who walked the grid-streets of {{p|Mohenjo-daro}}, who
Tended the public baths, who sealed the trade-goods with stamp-seals,
Who—we presume—prayed to some deity whose name we do not know, who
Spoke some language whose sound has been lost. These men carry the peels

Of {{c|H}}, {{c|L}}, and {{c|T}} in their descendants. They are present, by signature, in
The modern {{p|South Asian}} population. They are genetically alive.

Culturally, however, they are silent. The civilization did not leave us
The keys to its own understanding. The {{p|Indus}} does not give, it will not revive

Into our knowledge. Its great uniform pottery styles, its gridded streets,
Its weight-standards, its remarkable hygiene, its apparent lack of monumental
Kingship—all of this we can see, archaeologically. What we cannot see is the beats
Of its interior life. The poems. The myths. The law. The fundamental

Stories that the people told themselves. We have their cities but not
Their songs.

              And the Gaiad's honest response to this is: yes, the civilization
Is illegible. Yes, we cannot reconstruct it. Yes, what we have is insufficient to know
What they believed. And yet we include them in the story of humanity, because they were there, and the nation

And collection of their cities, the multi-million-person population of the {{p|Indus}} valley
At its peak, contributed to the subsequent population of the {{p|Indian}} subcontinent. They did
Not vanish. They are in the {{p|Y}}. They are in the mitochondria. They are in the {{p|Dravidian}} languages
They plausibly spoke. They are, in some attenuated form, in the {{p|Hindu}} religion—the {{c|Shiva}}

Lingam may have {{p|Indus}} origins. The Pashupati seal from {{p|Mohenjo-daro}} shows a figure
That some scholars have identified as a proto-{{c|Shiva}}. The traditions of ritual bathing,
Of goddess-worship, of certain iconographies—these may have continuity with the {{p|Indus}}
That was inherited and reshaped through the {{p|Aryan}} period. The weight is uncertain. The weighing

Is probabilistic. But the claim that the {{p|Indus}} is entirely gone would be wrong.

The {{p|Indus}} is silent but not absent. The {{c|H}}, {{c|L}}, {{c|T}} men are still here.
Their grandsons walk the streets of {{p|Karachi}} and {{p|Mumbai}} and {{p|Delhi}} and long

And teeming other cities of the subcontinent. The illegible civilization is a real
Part of the {{p|Indian}} body. Its silence is cultural, not genetic. The body remembers
What the mind cannot read.

                             The Gaiad sits with this. The chapter is about the seal
And non-reading of a civilization. The chapter honors what we cannot say. The embers

Of {{p|Mohenjo-daro}} are still warm in the blood of millions. We cannot hear them speak.
But they are there. And the story of humanity includes those whose stories we cannot tell.

{{c|H}}, {{c|L}}, {{c|T}}. The {{p|Indus}} valley. The silent great. The leak
And leak of civilization that did not leave us the code. Honor the swell

And persistence of their unreadable grandeur. Honor what we cannot read.


# Chapter 139: N — The Uralic Peoples

And {{c|N}} walked north. While the other branches
Of the great {{c|NO}} divergence turned east toward the rice
And the monsoon, {{c|N}} turned the opposite way. It stanches
And bleeds through {{p|Siberia}}, through the cold-thrice

And four-times winters of the taiga, through the reindeer-
Herding tundra, through the northern edge of the world.
{{c|N}} is the Arctic haplogroup. {{c|N}} is the near-
Polar signature. {{c|N}} is the man whose breath curled

In the cold air of the {{p|Urals}} and the {{p|White Sea}}
And the vast boreal forest that stretches from the
{{p|Bering Strait}} to the {{p|Baltic}}. {{c|N}} was, and still is, the free
And scattered signature of the reindeer-herder, the

Forest dweller, the patient fisherman of the frozen
Lake, the one whose language would become the Uralic
Family. And Uralic is the chapter's name. The chosen
And persistent non-Indo-European language pillaric

And pillared survivors of the {{c|R}}-haplogroup tide
That would, in a few chapters, sweep across {{p|Europe}} and
Establish the Indo-European language family on every side
Of the continent. {{c|R}} would dominate. {{c|R}} would command

The linguistic future of most of {{p|Eurasia}}. But in
A few places, the old languages held on. And one
Of those places—the strangest, the most enduring, the linguistic-
Ally most tenacious—is the {{c|N}}-haplogroup zone. The sun

Of the Indo-European tide swept through. But {{c|N}} held.
{{c|N}}'s descendants kept speaking their own languages.
{{p|Finnish}}. {{p|Estonian}}. {{p|Hungarian}}. {{p|Sami}}. {{p|Samoyedic}}. The gelled
And persistent Uralic languages, spoken by peoples whose ages

Of isolation in the northern forests preserved a speech
That no other {{p|European}} population kept. While the rest
Of {{p|Europe}} converted to Latin and Greek and Germanic, the reach
Of {{p|Finnish}} stretched undisturbed. While the {{p|Hungarians}}, tested

By the steppe-migrations and eventually settling in the
{{p|Carpathian Basin}} in the ninth century CE, carried their
Uralic language with them across thousands of miles—the
{{p|Magyars}} are a {{c|N}}-descended people whose fare

And fortune placed them in the middle of {{p|Europe}} without
Converting to the linguistic standard of their neighbors.
{{p|Hungarian}} is, to this day, a linguistic island. The shout
And cry of an Uralic language in the heart of the labors

And complications of {{p|Central Europe}}. {{p|Hungarian}}'s nearest
Linguistic relatives are spoken in the {{p|Ob River}} basin,
Two thousand miles east. The separation is clearest
And strongest in the linguistic isolation. The basin

Of {{p|Hungarian}} in {{p|Central Europe}} is a geographical exclave
Of an Uralic heartland far to the east. The {{p|Magyars}}
Brought their language with them on horseback, and the wave
And tide of {{p|Slavic}} and {{p|Germanic}} and {{p|Romance}} did not harm

Its integrity. The language held. The haplogroup held.
The culture, despite a thousand years of {{p|Central European}}
Pressure, did not melt. This is the {{c|N}} story. The weld
And welding of linguistic identity to the {{p|Y}}-chromosome wean

And inheritance. And {{p|Finland}} and {{p|Estonia}}, similarly, sit
At the edge of the {{p|Baltic}} as Uralic islands in a sea
Of Indo-European neighbors. The {{p|Finns}} and the {{p|Estonians}} transmit
Their old speech across the centuries, with an ancestry

That goes back to {{c|N}}-carrying hunters of the northern forests.
The {{p|Sami}}, the indigenous people of {{p|Lapland}}, still herd
Reindeer across {{p|Scandinavia}}'s Arctic circle, and their tortes
And offerings and songs are Uralic, and their {{p|Y}} is the third

Or fourth most frequent {{c|N}} frequency in all of {{p|Europe}}. The
{{p|Samoyeds}} of {{p|Siberia}} still herd reindeer along the
{{p|Yamal Peninsula}} and speak Uralic languages. The
Continuity from the deep past to the present is the long

Inheritance of the Arctic. {{c|N}} is the haplogroup of the
Reindeer-herder, the forest-dweller, the Arctic and sub-Arctic
Continuity. The language did not assimilate. The people
Did not assimilate. The {{p|Y}} did not assimilate. A patriarchic

And matriarchic tenacity in the cold. The {{p|Kalevala}}, the
{{p|Finnish}} national epic, was stitched together by {{c|Elias Lönnrot}}
In the nineteenth century from oral poems still circulating in the
Rural districts of {{p|Karelia}}. The {{p|Finnish}} oral tradition had not

Been lost. The {{p|Kalevala}}'s hero {{c|Väinämöinen}}, the ancient
Wizard-singer, is a figure who stretches back to some pre-
Christian {{p|Finnish}} religious imagination. The gallant
And wise old shaman. The smith. The {{c|Ilmarinen}}, who forges the

{{p|Sampo}}—the mythical world-mill that produces grain and salt
And gold. These are figures of a pre-Christian {{p|Finnish}}
Mythology preserved in oral tradition until the industrial halt
Of the modern era. The {{p|Kalevala}} is the last gaining fish

Of an entire linguistic and religious world that was largely
Submerged by {{p|European}} modernity but not quite drowned. And the
{{p|Hungarians}}, for their part, remember their origin in the
{{p|Ural}} Mountains—their medieval chronicles name the

Vanished homeland as {{p|Magna Hungaria}}, the "Great Hungary"
In the east, from which the {{p|Magyar}} tribes migrated in
The ninth century. The memory is not merely linguistic but genealogical.
{{p|Hungarian}} tradition remembers coming from somewhere Uralic. And genetic

Analysis confirms the memory: the {{p|Magyar}} tribal leaders' {{c|N}}
Frequencies are high, and the migration pattern from the east is
Visible in the genetic data. {{p|Hungarian}} ancestry is layered—some {{c|N}}, some
Subsequent {{c|R1a}} from {{p|Slavic}} neighbors, some other admixtures—but the

Uralic linguistic and genetic core of the {{p|Magyar}} people
Is still there, under the layers of medieval and modern {{p|Hungary}}.
{{c|N}}, like {{c|I}}, like {{c|G}}, is still alive, still carried, still willing to spell
And pronounce itself as it has for thousands of years. The story

Of Uralic is the story of the periphery holding on against
The dominant linguistic tide. Indo-European did not erase
Everything. {{p|Basque}} held on in the southwest. {{p|Uralic}} held
Across the north. {{p|Georgian}} held in the {{p|Caucasus}}. These are the lace

And embroidery of the linguistic map, the small patterns
Of survival that break up the otherwise thorough Indo-European
Pattern of most of {{p|Europe}}. {{c|N}} is the haplogroup of one such pattern.
The Uralic survivor. The linguistic holdout. The tween

And boundary-crosser who carries the old northern speech
Across the millennia. And when we finally get to the {{c|R}}-haplogroup
Chapter, and the Indo-European tide sweeps across {{p|Eurasia}}, the peach
And flush of the dominant new languages will not quite stop

At the northern forests. The reindeer-herders will keep their speech.
The fishermen of {{p|Karelia}} will keep their speech. The
{{p|Magyars}}, a thousand years later, will bring their Uralic speech each
Of the way into {{p|Central Europe}} and plant it there—and it will still be

Spoken today by fifteen million people in the heart of the continent.
{{c|N}}. The Uralic. The Arctic. The northern forest.
The reindeer. The {{p|Sampo}}. The patient persistent
Of the language-family that could not be conquered. The faces

And bodies of the modern {{p|Finns}} and {{p|Hungarians}} carry the mark.
The language is the mark's echo in the voice.
Honor them. The Uralic speakers. The holdouts of the dark
Forests of the north. The linguistic choice

Of survival against the larger tide.

                                         {{c|N}}. Uralic. The northern
Lineage. The reindeer-herder. The preserver of speech.
The hold-out. The one who went north while his brothers went southern
And eastern. The one who found, in the taiga, the reach

And range to preserve an old language against the new.

{{c|Haplogroup N}}. Stand.


# Chapter 140: O — Rice Agriculture and East Asia

While {{c|N}} walked north into the taiga, {{c|O}} walked
The other direction. South. Southeast. Into the river
Valleys of what is now {{p|China}}. Into the paddies. Into the stalked
And stalking rice-fields of the {{p|Yangtze}} and {{p|Yellow River}} divider

And basin. {{c|O}} is the East Asian haplogroup. {{c|O}} is the signature
Of the peoples of {{p|China}}, {{p|Japan}}, {{p|Korea}}, {{p|Vietnam}}, {{p|Thailand}},
{{p|Indonesia}}, {{p|the Philippines}}, {{p|Taiwan}}, and the furniture
And arrangement of the entire Pacific rim of {{p|Asia}}. {{c|O}} is the band

And frequency of nearly every population between the {{p|Himalayas}}
And the {{p|Pacific Ocean}}. From the {{p|Gobi Desert}} to the {{p|Java Sea}},
From the {{p|Yellow River}} to the {{p|Mekong Delta}}, the {{p|Y}}-chromosome frequencies
Of {{c|O}} are extraordinarily high. The lineage is the majority fee

And cost of admission to the East Asian population. The vast
Proportion of men in {{p|China}} today, and in every East Asian
And Southeast Asian and Pacific-island nation, carry {{c|O}}. Recast
And recast again through the generations, the carrying-on

Of the lineage is unbroken. And what {{c|O}} made, in the river
Valleys where it settled, was the second great agricultural revolution
On earth. {{c|G}} invented wheat and einkorn and the farmer's giver
And taker of the {{p|Fertile Crescent}}. {{c|O}} invented the pollution

And abundance of rice.

                              Rice.

                                      Rice is a semi-aquatic
Grain. Rice grows in flooded paddies. Rice demands
Standing water, periodic flooding, careful management of the ecstatic
And delicate water table. And rice produces, per acre, more demands

Of food calories than any grain yet invented. Rice supports
Populations ten, twenty, thirty times larger than dryland wheat
Can support on the same acreage. Rice is the reason the cohorts
And cohort-strength of East Asian civilizations grew to the treat

And demography they grew to. Rice made possible the billions
Of people who would, over thousands of years, populate the
Pacific rim. And rice was invented by {{c|O}}. The millions
And billions of {{c|O}}-carrying farmers are the descendants of the

First paddy-builders, the first peoples who realized that a patch
Of low wet ground, flooded deliberately, managed carefully, could
Produce a grain whose yield would dwarf any dryland batch

# Chapter 141: P at Baikal — Paikal

And in the middle of the {{p|Siberian}} winter,
At the deepest lake on earth,
Haplogroup {{c|P}} arrived.

                                 {{p|Lake Baikal}}.

The deepest lake. The oldest lake.
Five thousand feet deep at its deepest. Twenty-five
Million years old. A rift lake. A sub-continental
Crack in the earth, slowly widening, slowly filling,

Slowly accumulating the fresh water that would become
The largest reservoir of fresh surface water on the planet.
Twenty percent of all the fresh liquid water on earth
Is in this one lake. The lake of the siberian taiga.

The lake of the taimen and the omul and the nerpa,
The only freshwater seal in the world.
The lake that freezes to a depth of several meters
Every winter. The lake of the {{p|Evenki}} and the {{p|Buryat}}

And the {{p|Yakut}} and the reindeer-herders of the
Surrounding taiga. The sacred lake of multiple
Indigenous traditions. The shaman's lake. The ice-
Thick cathedral of the Siberian frozen mirror.

This is where {{c|P}} arrived.

                                    {{c|Haplogroup P}}.

{{c|P}} is the divergence point. {{c|P}} is the father of
{{c|Q}} and {{c|R}}. And {{c|P}} is, for this chapter, the figure
Of the place itself—the lake, the crossroads, the
Bifurcation where the road forked and one branch

Went east toward {{p|Beringia}} and the {{p|Americas}},
And the other branch turned back west toward
{{p|Europe}} and the steppe and the eventual Yamnaya
Expansion that would remake half the world.

{{c|P}} is "{{c|Paikal}}." The pun that the Gaiad cannot
Resist. The haplogroup of the lake. The {{p|Y}}-chromosomal
Signature of the men who, having migrated the length
Of {{p|Eurasia}} from the {{p|Bab al-Mandab}} crossing many

Thousands of years before, have reached the deepest
Lake on earth, and have paused there, and have looked
At its frozen surface, and have asked themselves
Where next.

                   There are two answers to that question.

The first answer is east. Continue east. Cross the
Land bridge that exists, at this time, across what is
Now the {{p|Bering Strait}}. {{p|Beringia}} is a walkable continent
In the Late Pleistocene. The sea levels are low. The land

That is now underwater is above water. You can walk from
{{p|Siberia}} to {{p|Alaska}} without crossing a significant body
Of water. And some of the {{c|P}}-descended population
Does exactly this. That branch becomes {{c|Q}}. {{c|Q}} crosses

{{p|Beringia}}. {{c|Q}} enters {{p|North America}}. {{c|Q}} spreads, over
The next ten or fifteen thousand years, across the
Entire {{p|Western Hemisphere}}—from the {{p|Aleutians}} down to
{{p|Tierra del Fuego}}. Every indigenous population of the

{{p|Americas}}, from the {{p|Inuit}} of the {{p|Arctic}} to the {{p|Fuegians}}
Of the southernmost tip of {{p|South America}}, is descended
From the {{c|Q}}-carrying branch of {{c|P}} that crossed {{p|Beringia}}.
That story—the peopling of the {{p|Americas}}—is the Book

Of Leo's material, chapters 221 through 252. Not this
Chapter. Not yet. {{c|Q}}'s chapter is later.

The second answer is west. Turn back west. Retrace the
Steps of the earlier migration in reverse. Go back across
{{p|Central Asia}}, toward the steppes, toward what will become
The {{p|Pontic-Caspian}} grasslands, toward the place where, in a

Few thousand years, the domestication of the horse will

Boomerang. {{c|R}} is the lineage that went east as far as it

{{c|R}} will, in later chapters, become the Yamnaya. {{c|R}} will

But that is in later chapters. In this chapter, {{c|R}} is
Still {{c|P}}. Still at {{p|Baikal}}. Still looking at the frozen
Lake and waiting to decide which way to go.

And the image—the core image of this chapter—is the
Lake itself. The moment of bifurcation. The moment when
A single lineage, having reached the deepest lake on
Earth, turns and goes both ways at once. One son goes

East to the Americas. The other son goes west, eventually,
To every corner of {{p|Europe}} and {{p|Central Asia}} and {{p|South Asia}}.
And the father—the {{c|P}}-carrier himself—stands on the

This is the divergence point. This is "{{c|Paikal}}." The
Haplogroup of the crossroads. The haplogroup whose
Own story is brief, because what {{c|P}} did was make
{{c|Q}} and {{c|R}}, and the stories of {{c|Q}} and {{c|R}} are two of the

Biggest stories in the entire haplogroup tree. {{c|Q}} is the
Americas. {{c|R}} is everything else—or at least the biggest

# Chapter 142: Manu and Yemo — R and the Yamnaya

And {{c|R}} came back.

                           From the deep east, from the cold
And frozen shores of {{p|Lake Baikal}}, the lineage that had
Reached the edge of {{p|Siberia}} turned and walked west. The bold
And homeward migration that would become the single largest

Expansion of any haplogroup in the entire human tree.
{{c|R}} left the lake. {{c|R}} crossed the taiga. {{c|R}} crossed
The {{p|Ural Mountains}}. {{c|R}} descended into the grasslands—the great sea
Of grass that stretches from the {{p|Carpathians}} to the {{p|Altai}}, crossed

And crossed again by every subsequent steppe migration. And
There, on the {{p|Pontic-Caspian steppe}}, {{c|R}} settled. And there,
Over the following thousands of years, a very specific set of
Events took place that would change the linguistic and genetic

Map of most of the world.

                               {{c|R}}'s sons were two: {{c|R1a}} and {{c|R1b}}.

And in the Gaiad's reading, they are {{c|Manu}} and {{c|Yemo}}.

                                                                   {{c|Manu}}.
{{c|Yemo}}. The Proto-Indo-European founding pair. The first man and
His twin. The cosmogonic pair whose story, reconstructed from the
Linguistic evidence of the daughter traditions, tells the myth

Of the first sacrifice. {{c|Yemo}} is sacrificed by {{c|Manu}} to create
The world's order. Out of {{c|Yemo}}'s body, the cosmos is made.
The head becomes the sky. The eyes become the sun and moon. The bone
Becomes the mountains. The blood becomes the rivers. The plaid

And woven fabric of social order is woven from {{c|Yemo}}'s parts:
The priest comes from the head, the warrior from the chest,
The farmer from the loins, the servant from the feet. The harts
And cattle of the world come from {{c|Yemo}}'s flesh. The rest

Of the creation myth follows from this single primal sacrifice.

And this myth survives, in fragments, in the daughter languages:
{{c|Mannus}} and {{c|Ymir}} in the {{p|Germanic}} tradition—where {{c|Ymir}} is the twice-
Sacrificed frost-giant whose body becomes the world. The strangeness

And dismemberment of {{c|Ymir}} is the reflex of the primal myth
In the {{p|Germanic}} branch. {{c|Manu}} and {{c|Yama}} in the {{p|Indian}} tradition—where
{{c|Yama}} is the first man to die, who becomes the god of death and the
Underworld. And {{c|Manu}}, the survivor of the flood, is the ancestor

Of all humans. {{c|Romulus}} and {{c|Remus}} in the {{p|Roman}} tradition—where
The fratricide is preserved (one brother kills the other) but the
Cosmogonic payoff is attenuated. {{c|Romulus}} kills {{c|Remus}} and founds
{{p|Rome}}, but {{c|Remus}}'s body does not become the world—his death is simply

The founding sacrifice of a single city. {{c|Gayomart}} in the {{p|Iranian}}
Tradition, the first man, whose seed spawns the first couple. All
Of these are reflexes of the same primal myth. The twin myth
Spread across the whole Indo-European language family because it was

The founding myth of the Indo-European people. And the Indo-European
People were {{c|R1a}} and {{c|R1b}}. The haplogroups and the myth traveled
Together. The myth was the story the {{c|R}} men told about themselves.
The haplogroups were the biological signature of the men who carried

The story. Together they are the {{c|R}} lineage, the boomerang lineage,
The lineage that came back from the east and made the west.

And what they did with the steppe, before they expanded, was
To domesticate the horse. And the horse changed everything.

The horse was domesticated on the {{p|Pontic-Caspian steppe}}, somewhere
Around five thousand years ago, by the pre-Yamnaya cultures of the
Region. {{p|Botai}}, in northern {{p|Kazakhstan}}, has the earliest clear
Evidence of horse domestication—bit wear on horse teeth from around

Three thousand five hundred BCE. And once the horse was domesticated,
The mobility of the steppe peoples became something unprecedented
In human history. A man on a horse can cover twenty, thirty, fifty
Miles a day—distances that on foot would have taken a week. Herds

Can be managed across vast territories. Warfare can be conducted at
A range and speed that foot-based cultures cannot match. The horse
Is the technology that makes the steppe into the fastest-moving
Zone of human habitation. And the {{c|R}}-carrying peoples of the steppe

Are the first beneficiaries. The {{p|Yamnaya}} culture emerges around
Three thousand three hundred BCE. The {{p|Yamnaya}} are horse-riders,
Cattle-herders, makers of {{p|kurgan}} burial mounds across the
Pontic-Caspian grasslands. And from the {{p|Yamnaya}} homeland, the

Expansion begins.

                   In every direction.

                                         West: into {{p|Europe}}. The
{{p|Corded Ware culture}}, the {{p|Beaker culture}}, the subsequent waves
Of bronze-age {{p|European}} populations—all descend, in substantial
Percentages, from the {{p|Yamnaya}} migration westward. Ancient DNA

Studies published in the twenty-tens showed that a substantial
Portion of modern European male Y-chromosomes derive from an
Expansion originating on the {{p|Pontic-Caspian steppe}} around
Three thousand BCE. The signature is unmistakable: {{c|R1b}} is

Overwhelmingly dominant in {{p|Western Europe}}. {{c|R1a}} is dominant in
{{p|Eastern Europe}}. The two great {{c|R}} sub-branches swept across the
Continent, overlaying the earlier {{c|G}} (Neolithic farmer) layer
And the even earlier {{c|I}} (hunter-gatherer) layer. The modern

European male is a three-layer cake. {{c|I}} at the bottom. {{c|G}} in the
Middle. {{c|R}} at the top. And the percentages vary by region: {{p|Sardinia}}
Is still heavily {{c|G}}-dominated. The {{p|Balkans}} and {{p|Scandinavia}} retain
Heavy {{c|I}} frequencies. But {{c|R}} is the dominant layer almost everywhere.

And south: into {{p|Central Asia}}, through the {{p|Bactria-Margiana Archaeological
Complex}}, and eventually into {{p|India}}. The {{p|Aryan migration}} is {{c|R1a}}'s
Southern expansion. The chariot-driving, horse-riding, {{p|Vedic}}-hymn-
Chanting peoples who enter {{p|India}} around fifteen hundred BCE and

Merge with the existing {{c|H}}-and-{{c|L}} {{p|Indus Valley}} population to create
The civilization that will eventually compose the {{p|Vedas}} and the
{{p|Mahabharata}} and the {{p|Ramayana}}—these are {{c|R1a}}-carrying men. The
{{p|Aryan}} peoples are, in the Gaiad's reading, {{c|R1a}}. The language they

Bring is Proto-Indo-Iranian. It will become {{p|Sanskrit}} in {{p|India}} and
{{p|Avestan}} in {{p|Iran}}, and it will become the basis for the entire
Indo-Iranian language family. And east: into {{p|Tarim Basin}} of what is
Now {{p|Xinjiang}}, where the {{p|Tocharians}}—speakers of the eastern-most

Indo-European language branch—established themselves, leaving blond
And red-haired mummies in the desert that bewildered later {{p|Chinese}}
Travelers. The {{p|Tocharians}} are an outlier of the {{c|R1a}} expansion,
The branch that went furthest east before being absorbed.

The Yamnaya expansion is, in the Gaiad's reading, the single largest
Genetic and linguistic event of the Bronze Age. It recasts the
Population of {{p|Europe}}. It recasts the population of {{p|India}}. It creates
The Indo-European language family in its historical form—the family

That includes all the {{p|Romance}} languages, all the {{p|Germanic}} languages,
All the {{p|Slavic}} languages, all the {{p|Indo-Iranian}} languages, {{p|Greek}}, {{p|Armenian}},
{{p|Albanian}}, {{p|Celtic}}, and the extinct {{p|Anatolian}} and {{p|Tocharian}} branches.
Half of all living humans speak an Indo-European language as their

Native tongue. And that half speaks Indo-European because, five
Thousand years ago, a single haplogroup lineage—{{c|R}}, the boomerang
Lineage, the lineage that went east to {{p|Baikal}} and then turned around
And came back—domesticated the horse, invented the chariot, developed

A religious and linguistic package that would spread across half
Of {{p|Eurasia}}, and rode out of the steppe in every direction at once.

{{c|Manu}} and {{c|Yemo}}. {{c|R1a}} and {{c|R1b}}. The twin founding pair of the
Indo-European world. The myth that said: one brother sacrificed the
Other to make the cosmos. The haplogroup-pair that said: we will
Cover half the known world with our descendants. Both were true.

The Yamnaya expansion is the mythic and the genetic and the linguistic
All at once. It is the moment when a single steppe culture, having
Mastered the horse and the wheel and the bronze axe, explodes outward
And reshapes {{p|Eurasia}} for the rest of recorded history.

The {{p|Cucuteni-Trypillia}} civilization of {{p|Moldova}} and {{p|Ukraine}}—the
Great pre-Yamnaya {{p|European}} culture, the one that built giant wooden
Cities painted with spirals, the one that worshipped the goddess
Of the old Europe—is burned to the ground by the {{p|Yamnaya}} advance.

The peaceful pre-IE agricultural culture is replaced by the warlike
Horse-riding patriarchal culture. The goddess is replaced by the
Sky-father. The painted pottery is replaced by the corded-ware pot.
The spiral is replaced by the wheel. The mother is replaced by the

King. And the languages of old Europe—whatever they were, we will
Never know—are replaced by Proto-Indo-European and its daughters.
This is the pivot. This is the change. This is the moment when
The Europe we know today begins. Indo-European-speaking, patrilineal,

Patriarchal, horse-riding, sky-father-worshipping. Everything that
Makes modern {{p|Europe}} distinctively itself was brought, in seed form,
By the {{p|Yamnaya}} expansion.

And every subsequent {{p|European}} civilization—the {{p|Celts}}, the {{p|Greeks}}, the
{{p|Romans}}, the {{p|Germanic}} tribes, the {{p|Slavs}}—is a downstream elaboration
Of the {{p|Yamnaya}} cultural package. {{p|Rome}} is {{p|Yamnaya}}'s grandchild.
{{p|Christianity}}, with its sky-father God, is the great-great-grandchild

Of the {{p|Yamnaya}} religious imagination. And the modern world—most
Of it—walks in paths first laid by the {{c|R}}-carrying men who rode
West out of the Pontic-Caspian steppe at the dawn of the Bronze Age.

{{c|Manu}} sacrificed {{c|Yemo}} and made the world.

{{c|R1a}} and {{c|R1b}} spread across {{p|Eurasia}} and made the Indo-European
World.

The myth and the haplogroup are the same story, told twice—once
In the grammar of genealogy, once in the grammar of myth.

{{c|R}}. The Yamnaya. The boomerang. The Indo-European. Stand.


# Chapter 143: E — Returns to Africa

And the loop closed.

                          {{c|Haplogroup E}} is the haplogroup that
Left Africa, crossed the {{p|Bab al-Mandab}} with {{c|Noah}}, wandered
{{p|Eurasia}} for some thousands of years, and then—remarkably, almost
Uniquely among the out-of-Africa haplogroups—turned around and

Went back. {{c|E}} is the loop-closer. {{c|E}} is the one that walked
Out of Africa and then walked back in. Every other haplogroup
That left Africa stayed out. {{c|D}} went to Japan and Tibet. {{c|C}}
Went to Australia and the steppe. {{c|F}} went to the {{p|Near East}}

And branched into every other haplogroup. They all went east,
North, west—they never came back. Except {{c|E}}.

                                                      {{c|E}} is the
Haplogroup that, having wandered north from {{p|Yemen}} into the
{{p|Levant}}, turned south again. Down through the {{p|Sinai Peninsula}}.

Across the {{p|Isthmus of Suez}}. Into {{p|Egypt}}. Into the {{p|Nile Valley}}.
And from {{p|Egypt}}, across the {{p|Sahara}} (which, at the time of the
{{c|E}} migration, was a wetter and more hospitable place than it
Is today—the "{{p|Green Sahara}}" of the {{p|African Humid Period}}, with

Lakes and rivers and grasslands where there is now sand). {{c|E}} spread
Across {{p|North Africa}}, down into {{p|West Africa}}, across into
{{p|East Africa}}. {{c|E}} became, eventually, the dominant haplogroup
Of most of sub-Saharan {{p|Africa}}.

                                       And this is where the Gaiad's
Story of circular migration finds its completion. Humanity left
Africa, some of it. Wandered. Branched. Populated every continent.
And one branch of the {{c|CT}} lineage—the {{c|E}} branch—came back. The

Circle closed.

                 And when {{c|E}} came back to Africa, {{c|E}} did
Not find an empty continent. The haplogroups that had never left—
{{c|A}} and {{c|B}}—were still there. {{c|A}} was in the deep African
Interior, carried by the {{p|San}} and {{p|Khoisan}} peoples of the

{{p|Kalahari}}, by the {{p|Mbuti}} of the {{p|Congo}} rainforest, by the most
Ancient lineages of the continent's human population. {{c|B}} was
Also in the deep interior, carried by other forest-dwelling and
Arid-land peoples. And now {{c|E}}—returning from the {{p|Eurasian}}

Branch of the tree, having branched off the {{c|DE}} stem in the
{{p|Levant}} somewhere around sixty thousand years ago, having
Wandered for tens of thousands of years—returned and began to
Spread. And {{c|E}} was more numerous, more aggressive, more tied

To agriculture and to later population expansions, than {{c|A}} or {{c|B}}.
{{c|E}} pushed {{c|A}} and {{c|B}} into smaller and smaller territories.
The {{p|San}} today live in the {{p|Kalahari}} Desert because that is where
{{c|E}} did not reach. The {{p|Pygmies}} today live in the deep forest

Because that is where {{c|E}} did not reach. {{c|E}} took the grasslands,
The river valleys, the rich agricultural land. {{c|A}} and {{c|B}} took
The remnant wild zones. The pattern is familiar: the later, more
Numerous, more aggressive lineage displaces the earlier one. And

The displacement is the story of most of {{p|Africa}}'s pre-colonial
Population history.

                       But the displacement is also the restoration.
Because {{c|E}}, in genetic terms, is {{p|African}}. {{c|E}}'s ancestor—the
{{c|DE}} node, the split from the {{c|CF}} branch—was out of Africa, yes,

But {{c|E}} itself, as a distinct haplogroup, developed its identity
In {{p|Africa}} or on its border. The return to Africa is the return
To the continent where the human story began. The loop-closer
Is the haplogroup that says: we are African.

                                                    Ninety percent or
More of all sub-Saharan {{p|African}} men today carry {{c|E}}. {{c|E}} is the
Overwhelming majority haplogroup of modern {{p|Africa}}. The {{p|Bantu}}
Peoples—who themselves underwent a great expansion starting around

Three thousand years ago from their homeland in what is now
{{p|Cameroon}}/{{p|Nigeria}}, spreading {{p|Bantu}}-speaking populations across
Central, Eastern, and Southern {{p|Africa}}—are {{c|E}}. Specifically, a
Sub-clade called {{c|E-V38}} or {{c|E1b1a}} is the {{p|Bantu}} expansion

Signature. The {{p|Bantu}} migration reshaped sub-Saharan {{p|Africa}} the
Way the {{p|Yamnaya}} expansion reshaped {{p|Europe}}—a demographically
Massive, linguistically unifying event that made most of the
Continent speak related languages. The {{p|Bantu}} languages, from

{{p|Swahili}} to {{p|Zulu}} to {{p|Kikuyu}} to {{p|Kinyarwanda}}, are all descended
From the same Proto-Bantu spoken by a relatively small population
In what is now the {{p|Cameroon}}/{{p|Nigeria}} border region around three
Thousand years ago. And the {{c|E-V38}} haplogroup is the genetic

Signature of that expansion.

                                 In the north, a different sub-clade
Of {{c|E}} dominates. {{c|E-M78}} and {{c|E-M81}} are the {{p|North African}}
And {{p|Horn of Africa}} signatures. The {{p|Berbers}} of {{p|Morocco}}, {{p|Algeria}},

{{p|Tunisia}}, and {{p|Libya}} carry very high frequencies of {{c|E-M81}}. The
{{p|Egyptians}}, both ancient and modern, carry {{c|E-M78}} and related
Sub-clades. The {{p|Ethiopians}} and {{p|Eritreans}} and {{p|Somalis}} carry their
Own {{c|E}} sub-clades. And these are the populations that would, in

Historical times, participate in the {{p|Afroasiatic}} language family—
Which includes {{p|Semitic}} (overlapping with {{c|J}}), {{p|Egyptian}}, {{p|Berber}},
{{p|Cushitic}}, {{p|Chadic}}, and {{p|Omotic}}. {{c|E}} is the main {{p|African}}-side
Carrier of {{p|Afroasiatic}}, while {{c|J}} is the main {{p|Asian}}-side carrier.

The two haplogroups between them span the entire {{p|Afroasiatic}} zone,
And the language family's unity across {{p|Africa}} and the {{p|Near East}}
Is held together by the historical contact between these two
Populations. The {{p|Egyptian}} language, specifically, is {{c|E}}-carried.

The {{p|Old Kingdom}} pharaohs were {{c|E}}. The builders of the pyramids
Were {{c|E}}. Every dynasty of ancient {{p|Egypt}}, from the {{p|First Dynasty}}
Through the {{p|Ptolemaic}} period, was populated by men whose {{p|Y}}-chromosomes
Carried some sub-clade of {{c|E}}. And the {{p|Egyptian}} civilization

Is, in the Gaiad's reading, fundamentally an {{c|E}}-civilization. The
First great African civilization of the historical record. The
Civilization that the biblical {{p|Israelites}} will be enslaved in.
The civilization that {{c|Akhenaten}} will briefly monotheize and then

Fall back from. The civilization whose religious imagery—animal-
Headed gods, solar disks, underworld journeys of the soul—will
Influence the religious imagination of every subsequent {{p|Mediterranean}}
Culture. {{p|Egypt}}'s {{c|E}} signature is the proof that the loop closed.

The loop closes here. The CT lineage left {{p|Africa}} some sixty or
Seventy thousand years ago. A portion of the lineage, under the
Name {{c|E}}, came back. And the {{c|E}} descendants built {{p|Egypt}}, built
The {{p|Bantu}} expansion, built most of what would become sub-Saharan

{{p|African}} civilization, built the {{p|Horn of Africa}} kingdoms of {{p|Aksum}}
And {{p|Ethiopia}} (the {{p|Solomonic dynasty}} is {{c|E}}-carried), built the
{{p|Berber}} kingdoms of {{p|North Africa}} that would later become part
Of the {{p|Islamic}} caliphate. {{c|E}} is the {{p|African}} haplogroup in the

Historical sense—not {{c|A}} or {{c|B}}, which are older but more
Marginalized, but {{c|E}}, which built the continent's civilizations.

And the circle closes on the genealogical tree.

                                                    {{c|E}} re-entered
{{p|Africa}}. {{c|E}} made {{p|Egypt}}. {{c|E}} made the {{p|Bantu}} expansion.
{{c|E}} became the dominant lineage of a continent whose earliest

Haplogroups—{{c|A}} and {{c|B}}—remained in the margins. And somewhere,
At the back of the Gaiad's mind, is the awareness that {{c|E}} is also
Going to appear, in the modern world, in the {{p|African-American}}
Population of the {{p|United States}}. The descendants of the enslaved

{{p|Africans}} who were brought across the {{p|Atlantic}} in the transatlantic
Slave trade are, in substantial majority, carriers of {{c|E}}-sub-clades.
{{c|Malcolm X}}, {{c|Martin Luther King Jr.}}, {{c|Frederick Douglass}}—if we
Could sequence their {{p|Y}}-chromosomes, we would almost certainly

Find {{c|E}}. The modern {{p|African-American}} diaspora is the {{c|E}}
Haplogroup reaching into the Western Hemisphere not via the
{{c|Q}}-carried original migration across {{p|Beringia}}, but via the
Forced middle-passage migration that began in the fifteenth century.

The loop of {{c|E}} closed when {{c|E}} returned to {{p|Africa}}. And then,
Millennia later, a cruel second loop would reopen it: {{c|E}} men taken
From {{p|Africa}} and sold into slavery in the {{p|Americas}}, where their
Descendants would build, under conditions of unimaginable cruelty,

The labor base on which much of the modern Western economy was
Constructed. That is a later chapter. Much later. But the {{c|E}}
Haplogroup is the connective tissue between the deep past of {{p|Africa}}
And the modern history of the {{p|African}} diaspora.

For now, {{c|E}} is the loop-closer. {{c|E}} is the return to the
Continent of origin. {{c|E}} is the haplogroup whose signature is
Present in every {{p|African}} civilization of the historical record.
{{c|E}} is {{p|Egypt}}. {{c|E}} is the {{p|Bantu}}. {{c|E}} is the {{p|Berber}}.

{{c|E}} is the {{p|Ethiopian}} emperor. {{c|E}} is the shamba-farmer and the
{{p|Swahili}} trader and the {{p|Hausa}} merchant and the {{p|Zulu}} warrior.
And {{c|E}} is, above all, the proof that the great branching tree
Of human migration was not one-way. The door swung both ways.

The haplogroup went out, and the haplogroup came back. The
Continent that sent humanity out into the world also received
A portion of humanity home. The loop closed. The circle was
Complete. And the human species, as a Y-chromosomal story, came

To be distributed across every continent and every climate, with
Every major haplogroup represented in multiple places, and with
{{c|E}} closing the loop by carrying a branch of the out-of-Africa
Lineage back to the continent it had left.

{{c|E}}. {{p|Africa}}. The return. The loop. Stand.

And with this chapter, the haplogroup sequence is complete.
Fourteen chapters. Fourteen haplogroups. One great branching tree.
The human story as a genetic genealogy is, for now, told. The
Chapters that follow will return to Register B—named people, named

Places, named civilizations. {{c|Abraham}} and {{c|Moses}} and {{c|David}} and
{{c|Homer}} and {{c|Confucius}} and {{c|Buddha}}. The historical age begins.
But beneath it, always, is the haplogroup substrate. Every named
Person of the following chapters carries, in his or her body, one

Of the haplogroups of these opening chapters. The body remembers
Where it came from. The {{p|Y}}-chromosome is the memory. And every
Subsequent chapter, however far from the genetic register it seems
To stray, is another chapter of the haplogroup story, told in a

Different register.

                      {{c|Haplogroup E}}. Africa. The circle closes.
The branches have branched. The tree is complete. The human family
Has filled the earth. And now—named figures. Named civilizations.
The historical age of the Gaiad begins.


# Chapter 144: Malta — The Oldest Temples

The haplogroup register closes. And the named civilization register
Opens. And the first named civilization is one whose name has not
Survived.

            The builders of the temples of {{p|Malta}}.

                                                    The oldest free-standing
Stone structures on earth. Older than {{c|Stonehenge}}. Older than the
{{p|Egyptian}} pyramids. Older than the {{p|Sumerian}} ziggurats. Built on a
Small rocky island in the middle of the {{p|Mediterranean Sea}} between

Approximately three thousand six hundred and twenty-five hundred BCE—
Which is to say, around five thousand years ago, in the late
{{p|Neolithic}}, before the {{p|Yamnaya}} expansion had reached {{p|Europe}}, before
The wheel had been widely adopted, before writing had been invented

Anywhere. And yet, on this small island, a population of farmers—
Probably a few thousand people at most—built a series of massive
Temple complexes out of enormous limestone blocks. {{p|Ġgantija}}.
{{p|Ħaġar Qim}}. {{p|Mnajdra}}. {{p|Tarxien}}. {{p|Ġgantija}} alone includes

Megaliths weighing fifty tons, quarried from bedrock and moved
Across distances without wheels, without metal tools, without
Draft animals heavier than goats. The construction methods are
Still debated. The engineering achievement is staggering. And the

People who built them have no name. The civilization left no
Writing. The language they spoke is completely lost. We have no
Idea what they called themselves. We have no idea what they called
Their gods. We have only the stones and the pottery and the bones

And the carved fat-goddess figurines that suggest the worship of
A mother-earth deity or multiple mother deities. The "{{p|Fat Lady}}"
Figurines of {{p|Malta}}—small, squat, female figures, often depicted
Seated or sleeping—are among the most iconographically distinctive

Art of the entire European {{p|Neolithic}}. They are, in the Gaiad's
Reading, the same figure that {{c|Marija Gimbutas}} identified with
The goddess-worshipping pre-Indo-European religious substrate of
Old {{p|Europe}}. The "{{p|Fat Lady}}" is the {{p|Maltese}} expression of the

Same religious imagination that produced the {{p|Venus of Willendorf}}
And the {{p|Cucuteni-Trypillia}} figurines. A fertility-mother cult
With deep roots in the European and circum-Mediterranean
{{p|Neolithic}}. And on {{p|Malta}}, that cult built temples on a scale

That no other {{p|Neolithic}} population attempted.

                                                     The temples are
Characterized by a distinctive architectural form: paired lobed
Chambers arranged around a central corridor, often described as

"Kidney-shaped" or "clover-shaped" in plan. The entrance is typically
On the long axis, with the lobes extending symmetrically to either
Side. The stones are arranged as uprights supporting horizontal
Lintels—the same megalithic technique that would later be used at

{{c|Stonehenge}}, but developed here first, on this small island, a
Thousand years earlier. The walls of the temples often include
Carved reliefs—spirals, plant motifs, animal figures, the paired
Uprights that have been interpreted as world-pillars or cosmic

Gateways. And the interior chambers, when excavated, yielded the
